name: South African Bobotie
description: Bobotie, spiced minced meat baked under a savory egg custard, is widely considered South Africa's national dish, with real Cape Malay roots and a genuine sweet-savory character from dried fruit and curry spice.

name: South African Boerewors
description: Boerewors, a coiled, spiced sausage traditionally grilled at a braai, is one of South Africa's most iconic foods - real boerewors, not a generic sausage, carries its own specific coriander-forward spicing.
steps_detailed: Grill the boerewors over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, 12-15 minutes, until well browned and cooked through.

name: South African Biltong
description: Biltong, air-dried, vinegar-and-spice-cured meat, is South Africa's most iconic snack - real biltong, distinct from beef jerky in both its curing method and texture, isn't a smoked or sweetened product.
steps_detailed: Serve the biltong sliced or torn, as-is - it's already fully cured and ready to eat.

name: South African Potjiekos
description: Potjiekos, meat and vegetables slow-cooked in a round cast-iron pot over an open fire, is a genuine South African communal cooking tradition, the dish named directly for its pot.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and broth.
Cover and simmer very gently, without stirring, 45-50 minutes, until everything is tender - real potjiekos is traditionally left undisturbed in layers rather than stirred.

name: South African Chakalaka
description: Chakalaka, a spicy vegetable relish, is a genuine South African township dish, traditionally served alongside pap or bread.
steps_detailed: Simmer the carrot, bell pepper, tomatoes, jalapeño, and curry powder together 12-15 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still have some bite.

name: South African Pap
description: Pap (mieliepap), a stiff maize porridge, is South Africa's most essential staple starch, traditionally served alongside grilled meat and chakalaka.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring often, over low heat 15-18 minutes until very thick and no longer grainy.

description: Bunny chow, a hollowed loaf of bread filled with curry, is a genuine Durban invention reflecting South Africa's Indian community.

name: South African Malva Pudding
description: Malva pudding, a warm, spongy apricot-jam-based cake soaked in a sweet sauce, is a beloved South African dessert with real Cape Dutch roots.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, sugar, chopped apricots, melted butter, and milk into a batter.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 22-25 minutes until set and golden.
Poke holes in the warm cake and pour a little extra warm milk over to soak in.

name: South African Melktert
description: Melktert, a custard tart with a delicately spiced filling, is a beloved South African dessert with real Cape Dutch roots.
steps_detailed: Whisk the milk, sugar, egg, and cornstarch together and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, 8-10 minutes, until thickened.
Pour into a small baking dish and chill until set.
Dust with cinnamon before serving.

name: South African Koeksisters
description: Koeksisters, syrup-soaked braided fried dough, is a beloved South African sweet with real Cape Malay and Cape Dutch roots.
steps_detailed: Work the flour and butter with a little water into a firm dough.
Roll and cut into strips, braiding three together.
Fry until deeply golden, 3-4 minutes, then dip immediately into warm honey syrup while still hot.

description: Sosaties, skewered marinated meat with real Cape Malay curry-and-apricot flavoring, a genuine South African braai dish.
steps_detailed: Toss the beef with the curry powder and marinate 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers alternating with the apricots and onion.
Grill, turning, 8-10 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: South African Beskuit-Style Rusks
description: Beskuit, twice-baked buttermilk rusks, a genuine Afrikaans tradition, meant for dunking in coffee or tea.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, butter, sugar, and baking powder with a little water into a firm dough.
Shape into a small loaf and bake at 350F (175C) for 25 minutes.
Slice and return to a low 250F (120C) oven for 25-30 minutes to dry out completely, giving real rusks their characteristic hard, dunkable texture.
